title: Concentrating Viruses via PEG precipitation
author: Jozef Nissimov

steps_raw.instruction: Add 58.4 g NaCl to 1 L of 0.45 µm filtered lysate (or 0.2 µm filtered lysate depending on the type of virus and its size) and dissolve gently. Let it stand on ice or at 4°C at least for 2 h.
Distribute into four sterile 250 mL centrifuge bottles.
Centrifuge the bottles for 2 h at 5000 rpm (at 4°C) and retain their supernatant.
Combine the supernatant of the four into an autoclaved sterile 1 L glass bottle.

Add PEG 6000 (Sigma) for a final percentage of 10% (wt/vol) and dissolve gently (i.e. 100 g into a total of 1L). Let it stand on ice or at 4°C overnight (the longer at cool temperature the better the yield).
Divide into four sterile 250 mL centrifuge bottles and centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 50 min at 4°C. Discard supernatant and invert the tubes on paper towels for a few minutes.

Re-suspend each pellet in 3 mL of suitable buffer (phage buffer/phosphate buffer/Tris buffer), and combine the four into a total of 12 mL in a falcon tube and store at 4°C until ready to proceed with either CsCl gradient or CTAB DNA extraction protocols.
